messages:
eva: Heads-up: nightly eval (run id 2026-09-12_02) flagged a big regression for `summarizer-agent` on q4a-quantized build. Repeat-loop + invented citations in >6% of docs. :eyes:

sunil: Can you paste an example generation and the metric diff?

eva: sure — short sample from failing prompt: 
```
User: Summarize this article about the new transit policy.
Model: In 2023 the Transit Institute reported that 78% of riders prefer X. See Smith et al., 2021, Transit Policy Review. Transit Institute data: 2019-2022 shows ... 
--- repeated: The Transit Institute data shows ... The Transit Institute data shows ... The Transit Institute data shows ...
```
This violates facts (no such Smith et al. ref) and loops on the "Transit Institute" phrase.

eva: Metric delta from nightly: repeat-rate +5.9pp (baseline 0.8% -> 6.7%), hallucination score +3.2pp, ROUGE-L -2.3. Failed prompts: 312/5000 sample prompts.

maria: Huh. That exact increase lines up with the q4a kernel change we rolled to canary on 2026-09-11 23:40 (kernel v3.2.7). ops-bot posted the deploy then. :thinking_face:

ops-bot: deploy: kernel-v3.2.7 canary -> eng-ml-pool at 2026-09-11T23:40Z (rollback window 60m).

noah: Did we change tokenization or NV kernel memory layout in that release? Repetition often points at KV-cache reuse or past-key offset bug.

maria: Nothing intentional in tokenizer. The kernel change touched GEMM tiling + cache stride; I flagged kv-indexing tests but they were green.

sunil: Quick repro plan: 1) rerun a failing prompt with fp16 full-precision model (same weights) 2) run q4a with kv-cache disabled 3) compare logits / next-token probs. If kv index wrong we should see identical logits until mismatch point.

eva: I'm on step 1 now. Repro on local GPU (fp16) returns clean summary (no Smith citation, no loop).

eva: Step 2: q4a with kv-cache off -> generates clean too. With kv-cache ON + q4a we get the loop. So KV + quantization interaction is suspicious.

noah: Nice repro. Can you capture the decoder logits around the first repeated token and diff between fp16 vs q4a? A single token mismatch early can cascade.

eva: Pasted small diff snippet: 
```
idx 345: fp16 logits top3 = ["Institute": -1.2, "Transit": -0.3, "transport": -1.4]
idx 345: q4a logits top3 = ["Institute": -0.1, "Transit": 0.8, "transport": -1.1]
```
That boost to "Transit" in q4a seems like low-bit rounding pushed it above threshold repeatedly.

maria: That matches a known quantization bias where certain tokens' kernel accumulation produces positive bias under 4-bit packing with the new tiling. I can try re-running quant kernels with compensated requant scaling.

sunil: Short-term mitigation: disable q4a+kv-cache combo in nightly evals and prod canary (block route). Also add a filter that breaks loops if same token repeated >6 times (safety guard).

maria: I'll open an infra PR to gate q4a+kv on canary. Linking issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/6421

noah: Long-term: add unit tests that run decoding with kv cache across quant variants; and add a determinism test comparing top-k logits between fp16 and quantized builds for a small set of token indices.

ci-bot: ci: created job nightly-regression/quant-kv-smoke with tolerances; job triggered by @maria.

eva: Action items: (1) temporary rollback/gate q4a+kv on canary (maria) (2) add loop-break safety in runtime (sunil) (3) new unit/regression tests (noah + maria) (4) reproduce + collect logits for triage doc (eva). I've created an internal incident thread: https://redwood/ops/INC-2026-1993 (will attach logs).

sunil: Assign me to runtime change. I'll push a small guard: if same token repeated >6 and probability trending up for 5 steps, force-sample next token.

maria: Rolling back q4a canary now. ops-bot: please annotate rollback in the deploy log.

ops-bot: rollback: kernel-v3.2.6 restored to eng-ml-pool at 2026-09-12T00:55Z.

eva: Thanks all. I'll post a short triage note in the eval dashboard with failed prompt examples and add a summary to the model onboarding checklist before we re-enable q4a. :white_check_mark:

noah: Great root cause hypothesis. Once we have full logits corpus we'll decide if it's quant bias (fix in quant kernels) or cache indexing (fix kernel layout). Keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
